articles.title: COGENT: A Modular Cognitive Architecture for Agentic User Simulation
articles.description:
arXiv:2611.31559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based user simulation can support interface design, accessibility research, and interactive-agent evaluation, but standard computer-use agents are optimized for task completion rather than reproducing how people perceive, reason, and act. We introduce COGENT (COGnitive agENT), a modular cognitive architecture for simulating user interaction with desktop interfaces. articles.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
articles.description:
arXiv:2611.31427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? articles.title: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management
articles.description:
arXiv:2611.31498v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) requires lifelong insulin therapy, and reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for automated dosing in the UVA/Padova simulator. However, the decisions of RL controllers remain difficult to interpret. We present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework for evaluating pretrained insulin-dosing policies without retraining. articles.title_zh: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management

articles.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
articles.description:
arXiv:2611.31579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. articles.title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
articles.description:
arXiv:2611.31347v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Laya is an open decision model: given a text, a question and K named options with descriptions, it returns one probability per option in a single pass, and software may act on the answer unseen. articles.title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls
articles.description:
arXiv:2611.31554v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Code-executing LLM agents submit blocks of code that issue several API writes. If a block fails after some of its writes have taken effect, the agent rewrites the block and continues. articles.title_zh: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls

articles.title: Safe Autoformalization: Sufficiency and Necessity with Entailment Graphs
